payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every real number x, and every integer m, one has E_n(x + m) = E_n(x).

dependency_self_check.periodicity_used: Established period 1 invariance by direct floor-shift cancellation.
dependency_self_check.statement_match: Proved exactly that E_n(x+m)=E_n(x) for all integers n>1, all real x, and all integers m.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer m. Define E_n(x)=floor(nx)-sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k. We show E_n(x+m)=E_n(x).

For the first term, nx+nm differs from nx by the integer nm, so floor(n(x+m))=floor(nx+nm)=floor(nx)+nm.

For each k with 1<=k<=n, k(x+m)=kx+km differs from kx by the integer km, hence floor(k(x+m))=floor(kx+km)=floor(kx)+km. Dividing by k gives floor(k(x+m))/k = floor(kx)/k + m.

Summing this over k=1,2,...,n yields sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+m))/k = sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nm.

Therefore
E_n(x+m)=floor(n(x+m)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+m))/k
=(floor(nx)+nm) - (sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nm)
=floor(nx)-sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
=E_n(x).

So E_n is periodic with period 1 on real inputs, as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use floor(t+q)=floor(t)+q for integer q. Both floor(nx) and each floor(kx) shift by an integer when x is replaced by x+m, and the added nm terms cancel in E_n.

used_external_facts: Basic identity: for real t and integer q, floor(t+q)=floor(t)+q.
